topics.question: No. 2 Georgia at No. 6 Alabama, GameDay in Tuscaloosa, the last top-six collision before November — what does the loser actually lose?
topics.traditionalist: The loser of this game does not lose the season — it loses the margin. Georgia at 5–0 with a loss in Tuscaloosa still controls its SEC path through the title game; Alabama at 5–0 with a loss still owns the tiebreaker math the committee respects. What it loses is the right to stumble again before Atlanta.
topics.analyst: The market can't split them — Alabama -1.5 with a 55 total is the tightest big-game number of the season, and the line's life tells the story: sharp money hit Georgia -1.5 inside two minutes, then home buyback settled it back to Alabama. FPI says Georgia (No. 2), the composite says Georgia (No. 2 to Alabama's 6), and SP+ — as of Sep 27 — said Georgia +30.2 to Alabama +23.0. Everything points home-team-or-pick'em; nothing points comfortable.
topics.evaluator: Two rosters with real injury asymmetry: Georgia is thin at receiver (Canion and Blackshear questionable, Green out) while Frazier is cleared; Alabama's AK Dear is questionable and Michael Carroll doubtful on the line. Whichever quarterback is throwing to his second-read receivers in the fourth quarter decides a one-score game.
topics.what_settles_it: Saturday, 7:30 PM ET, ABC — and then the SEC tiebreakers in November.

topics.question: Pitt is 5–0, newly ranked, and starting a fifth-year transfer who has never started a college game. Is the season now a countdown or a comeback story?
topics.traditionalist: Hold the eulogy. Mason Heintschel earned that 5–0 with a seven-touchdown game against Miami (Ohio) and a 35–33 escape in Blacksburg, but Pittsburgh football has always been bigger than one quarterback. Holden Geriner drove two scoring trains in relief; the defense is the identity.
topics.analyst: The market already answered: title futures don't carry Pitt, and the composite has them 25th — the ranking was always roster-plus-schedule, not quarterback-inflated. North Carolina at Pittsburgh is a four-point line, which says the books think the floor is intact. Two data points decide it: Geriner's 8-of-12 relief sample, and theACC's easiest remaining path among 5–0 teams.
topics.evaluator: The honest read is that everything downstream changes: no seven-TD outlier games, more fourth quarters like Blacksburg. Geriner's first start comes against a North Carolina team that just gave up 37 to Notre Dame — as gentle an entry as the schedule allows.
topics.what_settles_it: Beat North Carolina with one turnover or fewer, and Pitt–SMU in November becomes the real ACC eliminator.

topics.question: A wide receiver at even money for the Heisman — is Jeremiah Smith's board price the market being smart or the market being lazy?
topics.traditionalist: Two non-quarterbacks have won this trophy since 2010. Two. Back-to-back 200-yard games — the first Ohio State receiver ever to do it — is historic, but history says the award is a quarterback's award, and the books know exactly what they're doing pricing the liability at +100.
topics.analyst: The price is defensive, not predictive: BetMGM +100, FanDuel +110, DraftKings +115 after +245–260 a week ago, with books openly exposed on early tickets. The Athletic's first straw poll has him as the runaway No. 1 and FOX's board ranks him first — the polling and the pricing agree, which is unusual. The structural risk is ballot-splitting with Julian Sayin, and the Week 6 catalyst is elsewhere: Keelon Russell at +750 hosts Georgia.
topics.evaluator: Watch the Georgia–Alabama outcome, not Ohio State–Maryland. If Russell four-touchdowns his way through a No. 2 defense, the QB tier consolidates behind him and Smith's even money looks very expensive.
topics.what_settles_it: November stages: Penn State and Michigan. Receivers need statement games late; quarterbacks get them for free.

topics.question: Missouri 45, No. 8 Florida 17 — one October Saturday or a real reordering of the SEC's middle?
topics.traditionalist: Homecoming blowouts of top-ten visitors are how programs announce themselves. Missouri jumped 25 to 14, Jamal Roberts ran for 211 and three, and Florida's price collapsed from +2000 to +3500 overnight. That is a weekend, not a season.
topics.analyst: The composite still ranks Florida (16) ahead of Missouri (14 by a whisker via the polls), and the futures market agrees — but the markets moved on the underlying number: Missouri outgained the Gators by 258 and held Baugh to 13 yards on 12 carries. The structural read: the SEC's realistic bid ceiling is narrowing to Texas, Georgia, and Alabama, exactly as the playoff audit's outside references keep saying.
topics.evaluator: Texas A&M at Missouri is now the tell. The Aggies' power rating (77.5, 17th) actually grades ahead of Missouri's (73.0) — the books hung Missouri -4.5 anyway. If the Tigers win that one, the reordering is real.
topics.what_settles_it: Beating Texas A&M, then closing the November ledger without a second loss.

topics.question: Dante Moore is trending 'the right direction' in concussion protocol — should UCLA game-plan for him or for Dylan Raiola?
topics.traditionalist: Lanning said what coaches say: recovering, trending right, must clear every step of the NCAA protocol. Until Moore is cleared by doctors, UCLA's defensive room prepares for both quarterbacks, because Oregon's offense changes shape, not quality, between them.
topics.analyst: Oregon -11.5 with a 59 total says the market barely cares which one plays — a two-score-plus number against a 4–0, 21st-ranked UCLA team built on the run (281.5 yards per game, No. 4 in the FBS). Raiola's relief line (289 yards, two scores at USC) is a real sample, not a mop-up stat line.
topics.evaluator: The trench is the actual question: UCLA rushes for 281 a game and Oregon just watched its defensive front control USC. If Moore plays and is a game manager in his first contact since the ambulance ride, UCLA's formula gets easier, not harder.
topics.what_settles_it: Wednesday's initial availability designation and Moore's contact clearance — the ACC-style interval reports land midweek.
